items.item_text: Basic Life Support (BLS) certification from the American Heart Association or American Red Cross required
CCTC (Certified Clinical Transplant Coordinator) certification within 1 year of hire required
Bachelor’s Degree – Graduation from an accredited nursing program with a B.S. degree required
Master’s Degree – Graduation from an accredited nursing program with a Master’s degree preferred
Minimum 2 years of related experience or training required
5 years of relevant RN experience with a combination of critical care and transplant coordinator experience required

This role will serve as Supervisor for Transplant Coordinators under the direction of the Transplant Nurse Manager.  Responsible for operational and supervisory leadership by overseeing daily workflows, ensuring regulatory compliance (UNOS, CMS, OPTN), managing staffing and schedules, guiding complex clinical decision‑making, mentoring and evaluating coordinators, supporting quality improvement and facilitating interdisciplinary communication, and partnering with the Nurse Manager to maintain program continuity, growth, and high‑quality patient care.  Clinical case management of the transplant recipient/ living donor involving all phases of the transplant process, from initial referral throughout patient follow-up.  This position requires an advanced level of expertise and overall understanding of organ transplantation for the organ type specified. Responsibility involves coordination of interdisciplinary medical care delivery system under the direction of the Medical Director; liaison functions with patient, family, medical staff, referring physicians, and insurance companies; individualized patient/family teaching; assessment of appropriate medical intervention for effective use of resources and quality assurance.  Additional responsibilities include data collection for clinical management and certification requirements, development of educational materials and programs for patients, nursing staff and physicians.  Develop clinical protocols, and policy and procedures.  Community education and public relations.  Transplant donor/recipient coordination and liaison function with organ procurement agencies.
Ability to case manage all aspects of a transplant patient’s medical care from initial evaluation through post-transplant follow-up
Broad understanding and knowledge of organ transplantation, including immunology, immunosuppression, rejection and other complications of transplantation, drug toxicity, and graft failure
Ability to communicate effectively with persons of various cultural backgrounds
Good verbal and written communication skills
Ability to interface effectively with patients and their families
Excellent organizational skills and proficiency in meeting deadlines
Ability to work independently and prioritize workload
Ability to manage numerous concurrent tasks in a high-stress environment and deal with change
Ability to effectively coordinate and assess patient care
Ability to act as a liaison with nursing staff, outside agencies, team physicians, referring physicians, patients, and families
Ability to teach about transplantation and medical management issues
